items.headline: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 15
items.summary: Oil rose as traders assessed risks for supplies from the Middle East and Russia.
items.author: Charles Gorrivan, Nathan Risser and Kanoko Matsuyama

items.headline: Stocks Fall in Run-Up to Fed as Yields Stay High: Markets Wrap
items.summary: Wall Street traders refrained from making riskier bets in the countdown to the Federal Reserve decision, with stocks falling as elevated oil prices drove bond yields to multi-year highs.
items.author: Rita Nazareth

items.headline: Gold Holds Below $4,300 as Traders Brace For Fed Decision
items.summary: Gold held Monday’s slump as disruptions to oil flows from the Middle East reinforced expectations the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates for the first time in three years.
items.author: Yvonne Yue Li

items.headline: Traxion Gets Tender Offer as Share Liquidity, Price Drops
items.summary: A company linked to Grupo Traxion’s Executive President Aby Lijtszain Chernizky plans to launch a tender offer for as much as 100% of the Mexican logistics company’s shares, giving investors a chance to sell amid limited trading in the stock.
items.author: Valentine Hilaire and Carolina Millán

items.headline: Copper Rises as Traders Weigh New Deliveries, Fed Rate Path
items.summary: Copper advanced as traders weighed easing supply squeeze and bets that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates for the first time in three years.
items.author: Eddie Spence

items.headline: US 10-Year Yield Rises to Highest Since 2007 as Fed Looms
items.summary: The 10-year US Treasury yield rose to the highest in almost two decades, the latest milestone in a bruising global bond selloff driven by booming capital investment and soaring energy prices that are exacerbating inflation.
items.author: Greg Ritchie, Cameron Fozi and Matthew Burgess

items.headline: Emerging Assets Extend Four-Day Slide as Oil, 5% US Yield Bite
items.summary: Emerging-market stocks and currencies fell for a fourth session as rising global bond yields and oil prices kept riskier assets under pressure.
items.author: Andras Gergely and Vinícius Andrade

items.headline: US Stocks Fall as 10-Year Yield Hits Highest Level Since 2007
items.summary: US stocks fell on Tuesday after the benchmark Treasury yield touched the highest level since 2007 ahead of a Federal Reserve interest-rate decision on Wednesday, when traders expect an increase.
items.author: Emily Forgash

items.headline: Carney Expands Tax Break to Broad Range of Investments
items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney is expanding the scope of a major investment tax write-off, adding oil and gas pipelines, oil production equipment, mining property and more to the list of assets eligible for immediate expensing in Canada.
items.author: Erik Hertzberg and Brian Platt

items.headline: Dutch to Propose Capital Gains Tax to Break Reform Deadlock
items.summary: The Dutch government will propose a capital gains levy next year, bringing the Netherlands in line with most European countries on how they tax wealth.
items.author: Patrick Van Oosterom

items.headline: Susquehanna Insider Trading Case Called Into Doubt by Judge
items.summary: A federal judge dealt a setback to Susquehanna International Group’s lawsuit claiming it lost tens of millions of dollars to insider trading on a Chinese regulatory crackdown, denying a request to keep the alleged traders’ accounts frozen.
items.author: Chris Dolmetsch and Bob Van Voris

items.headline: AI Will Be Biggest 'Misallocation' of Capital, Says Noble
items.summary: The debate over how far, and how fast, artificial intelligence is advancing poses a serious dilemma for tech executives. They’re keen to telegraph their concerns, but having plowed hundreds of billions of dollars into AI, they’re trying to calm people down without spooking investors and customers. George Noble, Managing Partner at Noble Capital Advisors and former Fidelity Fund Manager, discusses artificial intelligence bear cases amid concerns over AI safety. Correct: George Noble said AI will be the 'biggest misallocation in history.' Fixes headline (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Glencore Faces $2 Billion Suit as It Alleges Radiant World Fraud
items.summary: Glencore Plc accused Radiant World and associated companies of sending falsified invoices to lenders — just as a senior executive at the group of traders said they had filed a $2 billion lawsuit against Glencore.
items.author: Jack Farchy

items.headline: Brookfield Agrees Recapitalization of Center Parcs at $6 Billion Valuation
items.summary: Brookfield is nearing a recapitalization of Center Parcs in a deal valuing the British holiday park operator at about $6 billion, people familiar with the matter said.
items.author: Dinesh Nair and Swetha Gopinath

items.headline: US 10-Year Yield Rises to Highest Since 2007 Ahead of Fed Decision
items.summary: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day than "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: Radiant World Group Sues Glencore For $2 Billion, Executive Says
items.summary: Radiant World and Sapphire Minmetals have filed a lawsuit against Glencore Plc in Singapore claiming $2 billion in damages, according to a senior executive at the group of companies.
items.author: Jack Farchy

items.headline: Maduro Fixer Saab Pleads Guilty in US Money-Laundering Case
items.summary: A close financial fixer for ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro pleaded guilty in Miami to a money laundering charge related to the South American country’s food-import contracts and oil sales that violated US sanctions.
items.author: Fabiola Zerpa

items.headline: Venezuela Squeezes Banks as Higher Spending Tests Bolivar
items.summary: Venezuela’s central bank is moving to squeeze liquidity in the banking system in a bid to support the bolivar ahead of an expected boost in government spending.
items.author: Nicolle Yapur

items.headline: Bessent Defends Treasury's Bond Market Intervention
items.summary: US Representative Jim Himes (D-CT) questions US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent about the Treasury’s recent intervention in the bond market, arguing that the government’s actions distort free markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.headline: History Won’t Help Us Understand Kevin Warsh
items.summary: Why he might surprise us tomorrow.
items.author: Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway
